editorial_contributions.text: The author proves several results and states problems which relate properties on \(C(K)\), the Banach space of real-valued continuous functions on a compact, scattered space \(K\), with analogous properties on the Boolean algebra of all clopen subsets of \(K\). The author is especially interested in renorming properties: when does a given Banach space possess an equivalent norm with some ``good'' properties? Properties considered here include: \(\sigma\)-scattered, \(\sigma\)- fragmentable, Namioka, DN, and \(\sigma\)-discrete. (See the paper for definitions.) Among the questions the author asks, is, if \(X\) is a topological space which is not \(\sigma\)-scattered, does there exist a Baire space \(B\) and a continuous, nowhere constant map from \(B\) into \(X\)? The author notes that \textit{I. Namioka} and \textit{R. Pol} in a preprint [Mappings of Baire spaces into function spaces and Kadets renormings] have shown that this problem has a negative answer under the continuum hypothesis.

keywords: Boolean algebra of all clopen subsets
